ca_highlands_wall.blurb: Highlands Wall is the first cliff you pass on the way to Crystal Crag, above Lake George in the Mammoth Lakes basin, at roughly 10,000 feet. It faces northeast. Most of the 18 climbs are single-pitch bolted lines of about 90 to 110 feet on clean stone striped with quartz dikes, with a few trad lines and one two-pitch route mixed in. The grades sit mostly around 5.10, with a good number of 5.11s and a few 5.9s; nothing is easier than 5.8. It suits sport climbers who are comfortable on steady, sustained face climbing and want a high-altitude alternative to the valley crags.

ca_indian_rock_3.blurb: Indian Rock is a compact sandstone outcrop of around 30 feet, ringed by small boulders, in the Castle Rock and Sanborn area of the South Bay, close to Los Gatos. Routes run roughly 20 to 60 feet, mostly bolted, with a handful of trad lines and one boulder problem, and nearly everything can be top-roped. Grades span about 5.7 to 5.12, with a fairly even spread from 5.10 up to 5.12. Trees keep the base shady for most of the day while the tops catch sun. It is short and easy to reach, so it works well for a quick session, and it is a heavily used crag.

ca_main_wall_left_2.blurb: Main Wall Left is a short granite wall of about 30 feet at Belvedere Heights within the Box Springs Mountain Reserve, behind the university in Riverside. It faces southeast and is really two overlapping walls, with a smaller one behind and to the right that holds a few top-rope lines. The climbing is crimpy, a mix of bolted routes, moderate cracks and top-rope problems, with most grades from 5.7 to 5.11 and the bulk around 5.9 and 5.10. Most lines have their own anchor and an easy walk-off either side makes it good for top-roping, though it is low and warm rather than a destination crag.

ca_corral_wall_left_side.blurb: The left half of Corral Wall sits in Rattlesnake Canyon, in the Indian Cove part of Joshua Tree National Park. It is a mostly traditional crag with 18 climbs, a blend of crack and face lines plus a couple of top-rope options and a single bolted line. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, but the bulk are moderate, 5.8 to 5.10, with only a couple of harder ones. Bolted anchors up top make descents simple and let you lap many routes in a day. The wall is tucked out of the wind, so it is a sensible pick on cold, blustery days, and it fills up on weekends.

ca_north_face_8.blurb: North Face is the shady side of North Rock, one of the formations in the Footsteps Rock cluster on the Northwest California coast. It faces north and stays cool even in summer. The wall is known for quality slab climbing, and most of its 18 routes are bolted, with a few trad lines and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.7 and are spread across 5.8 to 5.12, with 5.10 the most common and a solid group of 5.11s. The Footsteps trail leads down to the notch above the formations, and from there you go past North Rock to reach this face.

ca_handley_rock_park.blurb: Handley Rock Park is a small hilltop park in the Emerald Hills neighborhood of Redwood City, centred on a sandstone outcrop about 50 feet high. It is mainly a top-rope venue: many of the 18 climbs are set up from above, and a walkable path on the far left side gets you to the anchors, so a good number of ropes can hang at once. A few sport lines and a couple of boulder problems up to V3 round it out. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, weighted toward 5.11 and 5.12. The streets around it are residential and parking is tight.

ca_got.blurb: GOT is a crag in Pine Creek Canyon above Bishop, at about 7,500 feet, between Crack of Noon Buttress and Cyanide Gully. It splits evenly between trad and sport, nine lines each, and the climbing is mixed in style. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.12, mostly 5.9 through 5.11, with 5.11 the most common. It gets sun from late morning through mid-afternoon. A short trail from the road leads to the cliff, then a scramble up and around the talus field gets you to the base, so expect a bit of loose ground before you rope up.
